clue.text: Flimsy material for padre's boat

indicators.note: something flimsy falls apart easily, so the letters of padre's boat collapse and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken with its S, as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman's boat is made of something too weak to float.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flimsy' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal: the letters of PADRES BOAT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasteboard is stiff card made of pasted sheets, a material used for boxes and models.

clue.text: Records for a pound, in old Asian coins

indicators.note: in places the pound symbol inside the word for the coins

parts.note: annas were small coins of British India, sixteen to the rupee
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Accounts of swapping old Indian coins for British currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside ANNAS; the 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are yearly chronicles, historical records kept year by year.

clue.text: Use it, Tom, to make a meal for yourself

definitions.text: Use it, Tom, to make a meal for yourself

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone urges a tomcat to catch a small bird for its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Tom is a tomcat, and a small bird is the meal it is told to make from the letters of USE IT TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tit is a small songbird a cat might catch and eat, the prey in the picture.

clue.text: Mole fixes leisure spell on the river?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes first, above it

parts.note: a break is a short spell of rest or leisure
the river is loosely the water

explanation.surface: An animal that burrows takes a rest by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' pretends to be the burrowing animal; it is a harbour wall. 'fixes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone pier or sea wall, the same structure as a barrier against waves.

clue.text: Destination of a wicked fellow!

parts.note: wicked means bad
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An exclamation about where an evil man ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: Abaddon is the bottomless pit or hell of the Bible, the place a wicked man is bound for.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Abaddon is the pit of destruction, the underworld where the damned end their journey.

clue.text: But it's no obstacle to a female impersonator

definitions.text: But it's no obstacle to a female impersonator

parts.words: But it's no obstacle to a female impersonator
parts.note: one word means a hindrance that slows you down, yet a man performing as a woman wears it, so for him it is no hindrance

explanation.surface: Nothing stops a pantomime dame from performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hindrance holding you back and women's clothing worn by a male performer.

clue.text: Hide from Billy the Kid? Could be on the bottle!

definitions.text: Hide from Billy the Kid? Could be on the bottle!

parts.words: Hide from Billy the Kid? Could be on the bottle!
parts.note: Billy the Kid sounds like the outlaw but is a billy goat and its kid; their hide, made into a wine bottle, is the leather

explanation.surface: An outlaw on the run who may also have taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy the Kid looks like the Wild West outlaw; read it as a billy goat or a kid, whose hide makes a wineskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Goat leather is used for wineskins, the traditional drinking bottle of herdsmen.

clue.text: Mint coin worthy of a king

parts.note: a penny is a coin
royal means fit for a king

explanation.surface: A newly struck coin fit for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like a verb about making coins; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a small European species of the herb family that includes spearmint.

clue.text: Flower-girl holds record for stillness

indicators.note: one word holds the other, so it goes around it

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name that is also a flower
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A girl named after a flower keeps a disc as a souvenir of calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 'I' after Flower-girl; the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is rest and calm, a state without movement.

clue.text: Stories the arts master found a curse

parts.note: ana are collected anecdotes or stories about a person
taken as written
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A graduate finds stories to be a dreadful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of sayings or anecdotes, is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ban by the Church, an excommunication pronounced as a malediction.

clue.text: Bad language to follow closely? The French can

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow at their heels
la is French for the (feminine)
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone tails a person who knows the French cancan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad language' sounds like swearing; it means poor Latin. 'The French can' also hints at the cancan dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog Latin is crude, ungrammatical mock Latin, a corrupted form of that classical tongue.

clue.text: He observed a hunter, it's said, down the Elephant

indicators.note: the Elephant and Castle is a district of south London, so this is a Cockney speaking, dropping the H as people do there

parts.note: he saw, said with the H dropped, becomes 'e saw

explanation.surface: Someone reports seeing a big-game hunter near a London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elephant and Castle is an area of south London; a Cockney there drops the H of 'he', so 'He saw' comes out as the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Esau, Jacob's brother, is described as a skilful hunter, a man of the field.

clue.text: Promptness required for warlike enterprise

definitions.meaning: speed and efficiency in doing something
a military campaign sent to a distant place

explanation.surface: Quick work is needed for a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means speed in getting things done and also a journey made by an armed force.

clue.text: Just the bird to go to Pinocchio's head?

definitions.text: Just the bird to go to Pinocchio's head?

parts.words: Just the bird to go to Pinocchio's head?
parts.note: Pinocchio is a puppet whose nose grows; a nose is slangily a pecker, and his is made of timber, so the bird's name describes it

explanation.surface: Asks which bird would attack a puppet's wooden head.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinocchio is a carved wooden puppet famous for his nose, and 'pecker' is slang for a nose; such a bird would also happily peck at his head.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird drills into trees for insects, so a timber puppet would suit it well.

clue.text: Condiment perfect for suckers

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is one sweet: peppermints are sweets you suck

parts.note: pepper is a condiment
in mint condition means perfect, as new

explanation.surface: A seasoning that is just right for gullible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suckers' suggests gullible people; it means sweets that are sucked.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint is a hard sweet flavoured with mint oil, made to be sucked slowly.

clue.text: Head accepts hire of painter's board

indicators.note: one word accepts the other, taking it inside

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
to let is to hire out

explanation.surface: A boss agrees to rent an artist's equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the thin board on which an artist mixes paints.

clue.text: Publicity handouts from the smaller branches?

definitions.meaning: printed sheets given out to advertise something
the small leaves on twigs, the subdivisions of a compound leaf

explanation.surface: Promotional flyers sent out by a firm's minor offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests local offices of a business; it means a tree's twigs, which bear small leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means printed handbills and also the small divisions of a plant's foliage.

clue.text: Steps nimbly back with marshal to the copse

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: to nip is to move quickly and nimbly
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Someone darts back with a military officer to a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIPS into SPIN; 'to the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a small thicket of trees, a little wood.

clue.text: A brief doze shortens this game

definitions.text: A brief doze shortens this game

parts.words: A brief doze shortens this game
parts.note: a short sleep is a nap, and that word is also the shortened name of the card game

explanation.surface: A quick nap makes a game end sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game Nap takes its short name from this longer one, named after the French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: This trick-taking card game is usually called by its short form, a word also meaning a doze.

clue.text: First male worker, unyielding to requests

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: The first man and a labourer both refuse to give in to pleas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to requests' merely completes the sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant is firm and immovable, refusing to be persuaded.

clue.text: As a means of protection it has its up and downs

definitions.text: As a means of protection it has its up and downs

parts.words: As a means of protection it has its up and downs
parts.note: a castle's defence over a moat that is raised and lowered, the idiom about mixed fortune taken literally

explanation.surface: Something defensive goes through good times and bad.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged bridge over a moat is raised to keep attackers out and lowered for entry.

clue.text: Stitch causes upset

definitions.meaning: a knitting stitch made by reversing the plain stitch
an old verb meaning to overturn or capsize

explanation.surface: A sewing problem leaves someone annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Purl names a reverse knitting stitch and also, in old use, to overturn or upend.

clue.text: Sound bases for travellers' courses

indicators.note: sound signals a word said aloud that is spelt differently

parts.note: roots are bases or foundations

explanation.surface: Solid foundations for the journeys travellers make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid; it is the homophone signal, and ROOTS and ROUTES sound the same in many accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Routes are the ways or paths travellers take.

clue.text: Message spread to allow retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the joined words are read in reverse

parts.note: marge, short for margarine, is a spread
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A note that is circulated to permit a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reverses MARGE + LET as a whole, giving TEL then EGRAM; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Upset at alternative duty cycle

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the two words together are read upwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a different schedule of duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns AT + OR as one run, giving the answer read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list setting out who takes each turn of duty in rotation.

clue.text: Liqueur for a musical group, say

definitions.text: Liqueur for a musical group, say

parts.words: Liqueur for a musical group, say
parts.note: the drink's name ends like quartette or sextette, so it could pass for a band of players

explanation.surface: Asks for a drink to serve a band.
explanation.walkthrough: Old spellings of small ensembles end in -ette (quartette, quintette), and this aniseed liqueur's name looks like one.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet liqueur flavoured with aniseed.

clue.text: Not in suitable gear

parts.note: not in means out
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone is not at home in the right clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes, and gear is informal for clothing.

clue.text: A sagacity associated with small fish? Just so

definitions.text: associated with small fish? Just so
definitions.meaning: in Kipling's Just So Stories the small 'Stute Fish is the clever one, so its quality is named after it

explanation.surface: Wisdom linked to tiddlers, exactly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just so' looks like agreement; it points to Kipling's Just So Stories, where the whale's tale features a small, astute fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness and cleverness are what the word means, the quality of being sharp-witted.
